headline: Nestlé agrees to sell the rest of Alcon to Novartis
text: On 4 January Nestlé agreed to sell its remaining majority stake in Alcon to Novartis, part of a $39.3 billion offer by Novartis for all of Alcon. Nestlé also agreed to buy Kraft's American frozen pizza business, including DiGiorno and Tombstone, for $3.7 billion.
imageCaption: Paul Bulcke, chief executive of Nestlé, Davos, January 2010

headline: Novartis bids for all of Alcon; Jimenez takes over
text: On 4 January Novartis agreed to buy Nestlé's remaining majority of Alcon, part of a $39.3 billion offer for the whole company. Daniel Vasella handed the job of chief executive to Joseph Jimenez and stays chairman.
imageCaption: Daniel Vasella of Novartis at the World Economic Forum, Davos, January 2010

headline: Apple announces the iPad
text: On 27 January Apple announced the iPad, a tablet computer with a screen twice the size of the iPhone's, without phone functions. It goes on sale in April.
imageCaption: Steve Jobs introduces the iPad, San Francisco, 27 January 2010

headline: Coca-Cola to buy back its North American bottler
text: Coca-Cola is in talks, announced on 24 February, to buy the North American business of its biggest bottler, Coca-Cola Enterprises, which delivers about three quarters of Coca-Cola's US bottler volume and almost all in Canada. In return CCE would take over Coca-Cola's own bottling operations in Norway and Sweden.

headline: Schlumberger buys Smith International for 11 billion dollars
text: On 21 February Schlumberger agreed to buy Smith International, a maker of drill bits and drilling fluids, in an all-share deal: 0.6966 Schlumberger shares per Smith share, a 37.5 percent premium, valuing the deal at about 11.3 billion dollars.
source: Schlumberger and Smith press release of 21 February 2010, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/000119312510035707/dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlumberger (value, completion) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Offshore drilling rigs being refurbished at Corpus Christi, Texas

headline: The iPad sells 300,000 on its first day
text: Apple's iPad, a tablet computer announced on 27 January at 499 dollars, went on sale in the US on 3 April and sold 300,000 units the first day. Apple is selling a whole family of touch-screen devices running the same apps.
imageCaption: Typing on the iPad at Apple's presentation event, San Francisco, January 2010

headline: Greece and the flash crash: shares fall 8 percent
text: After Standard and Poor's cut Greece's credit rating to junk on 27 April, fears about Europe's debt crisis gripped markets. On 6 May the Dow, already down more than 300 points, plunged almost 1,000 points within minutes in the afternoon, about 9%, before recovering most of it; roughly a trillion dollars of value vanished and reappeared within half an hour. The S&P 500 lost 8% in May to 1,089.41.
imageCaption: The Marfin bank branch in Athens after the riots of 5 May 2010

headline: Europe bails out Greece and sets up a rescue fund
text: On 2 May the eurozone countries and the IMF agreed a 110 billion euro loan for Greece, which can no longer borrow on the markets after admitting that its deficit was far larger than reported; Greeks protested in the streets against the spending cuts attached. A week later the EU created a European Financial Stability Facility with up to 750 billion euros to stop the crisis spreading to Portugal, Spain and others. On 6 May the Dow plunged 998 points, about 9 percent, mostly within minutes, before recovering much of the loss in a 'flash crash'.
imageCaption: A bank branch burned out during protests against the austerity programme, Athens, 5 May 2010

headline: IBM promises at least 20 dollars a share by 2015
text: At its investor meeting IBM set out a '2015 roadmap': operating earnings of at least 20 dollars a share by 2015, against about 11 dollars for 2010, growth from emerging markets, analytics and cloud computing, and 100 billion dollars of free cash flow, 70% of it returned to shareholders, including about 50 billion dollars of share buybacks.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000110465910027974/a10-9848_18k.htm (IBM 8-K of 2010-05-12 with the investor presentation, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Sam Palmisano, IBM's chairman and chief executive

headline: Apple is now worth more than Microsoft
text: On 26 May Apple's stock market value overtook Microsoft's for the first time since 1989. Apple sells iPhones and iPods; Microsoft's sales still depend on Windows and Office for PCs.
imageCaption: Steve Jobs with the iPad, January 2010

headline: The Gulf spill halts deep drilling
text: The Deepwater Horizon rig exploded on 20 April, killing 11 workers, and the well is still gushing tens of thousands of barrels a day into the Gulf of Mexico. The US government has imposed a six-month moratorium on deepwater drilling, stopping work on 33 rigs. US crude fell 14% in May to $74.
imageCaption: The Deepwater Horizon drilling rig on fire in the Gulf of Mexico, 21 April 2010

headline: Tesla, the electric car maker, goes public
text: Tesla Motors sold 13.3 million shares at 17 dollars on the Nasdaq on 29 June, raising 226 million dollars; it is the first American car maker to go public since Ford in 1956. Tesla builds the Roadster, an expensive electric sports car, and plans a family saloon, the Model S. It loses money; in May it bought the former NUMMI car plant in Fremont, California, from Toyota, which is buying 50 million dollars of Tesla shares.
imageCaption: A Tesla Roadster, the car Tesla sold when it listed its shares in June 2010

headline: BMW joins Europe's blue-chip index as car shares boom
text: German car makers are profiting from robust economic growth, and their shares are leading the DAX. In September BMW's ordinary shares were taken into the EURO STOXX 50 index of the eurozone's largest companies. The euro rose from 1.27 to 1.36 dollars during the month.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 2010, 'Automobile stocks boost DAX', https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2010.pdf (read 2026-10-03); FRED DEXUSEU, data/raw/fred/DEXUSEU.csv (read 2026-10-03)

headline: German car shares race ahead
text: German car makers are booming as the economy recovers; in July Daimler raised its profit target for 2010. In September stock markets rallied worldwide and German car shares led the DAX. The euro rose from 1.27 to 1.36 dollars during the month.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 2010, 'Automobile stocks boost DAX' (Prime Automobile index +56.5% in 2010), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2010.pdf (read 2026-10-03); Times of Malta, 'Daimler raises 2010 earnings target', 28 July 2010 (headline, via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); FRED DEXUSEU, data/raw/fred/DEXUSEU.csv (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Nokia fires its chief and hires Microsoft's Stephen Elop
text: On 10 September Nokia replaced chief executive Olli-Pekka Kallasvuo with Stephen Elop, head of Microsoft's business division and the first non-Finn to run the company, as it struggles to compete with Apple's iPhone and phones running Google's Android. In June Nokia had warned that phone sales would come in at the low end of its forecast.
imageCaption: Stephen Elop, formerly of Microsoft, named Nokia's chief executive

headline: Panasonic and Toyota deals send Tesla soaring
text: Panasonic, the world's leading maker of lithium-ion battery cells, bought 30 million dollars of Tesla shares at 21.15 dollars. Tesla's third-quarter revenue rose 10% to 31.2 million dollars and its loss narrowed to 34.9 million. At the Los Angeles motor show Toyota showed an electric RAV4 'powered by Tesla'. The shares closed at a record 35.47 dollars on 24 November, more than double the IPO price.
source: Tesla 8-K exhibits of 4 November 2010 (Panasonic) and 9 November 2010 (Q3 results), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312510248220/dex991.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312510254219/dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); The Mercury News, 'Tesla Motors stock shows strong gains since IPO', 26 November 2010, https://www.mercurynews.com/2010/11/26/tesla-motors-stock-shows-strong-gains-since-ipo/ (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Model S body in the Tesla factory, Fremont, California

headline: Treasury sells its last Citigroup shares, at a profit
text: The U.S. Treasury sold its remaining 27% stake in Citigroup, ending government ownership; taxpayers made an overall profit of about $12 billion on the rescue. Citigroup has been profitable in each of the first three quarters of 2010.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citigroup (read 2026-10-03, citing Reuters and Washington Post, 7 December 2010); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000110465911001741/a11-4145_1ex99d1.htm (read 2026-10-03)
